pamphlet_excerpts: Sheen Critical: Sheen is a critical characteristic that refers to the degree ofshine or gloss of any coating or surface.
Sheen Currently Onthe: The sheen currently onthe surface can determine the amount of surface preparationrequired.
Sheen Affects Performance: Sheen affects the performance of the finish coat: theabrasion resistance, chemical resistance, and overall beauty ofthe painted area.
Typical Full Sheen: The typical full sheen range, from lowest to highest, includes flat or matte, eggshell or low luster, satin or pearl, semigloss, and high or full gloss.
step_by_step_procedure: There Industrywide Standard: Because there are no industrywide standard definitions of these terms, gloss levels may vary from one manufacturer to another.
Type Sheen Choose: The type of sheen you choose will depend on what you arepainting.
Flat Finish Ceilings: A flat finish is most often used for ceilings and oninterior walls.
Not Washable Paints: It is not as “washable” as paints with moresheen.

pamphlet_excerpts: Applying Primer Coat: Applying primer, the first coat of paint, also is the last stage ofsurface preparation.
Primer Next Coat: The primer makes the next coat stick to thesurface, protects the substrate, and seals the surface.
There Aredifferent Primers: There aredifferent primers for wood, concrete and masonry, plaster anddrywall, steel, and other metals.
Wood Primers Available: Wood primers are available in oil-based orwater-based products and can be used indoors or outdoors.
step_by_step_procedure: Exterior Masonry Surfacesare: Exterior masonry surfacesare often highly alkaline, so be sure to use primers on surfacesthat are alkali-resistant.
Primers Plaster Surfaces: Make sure primers for plaster surfaces are alkali-resistant and that plaster dust is removedfirst.
Primers Drywall Gypsum: The best primers for drywall or gypsum board are waterbased, such as vinyl and acrylic.
Type Primer Choose: The type of primer you choose depends onthe surface preparation required as well as the topcoat to beapplied over the primer.

pamphlet_excerpts: Color Wheel Illustrates: The color wheel illustrates how colors blend together.
Traditional Color Wheel: On the traditional color wheel shown here, you can see that the primarycolors form a triangle.
Secondary Colors Form: The three secondary colors form a secondtriangle.
Intermediate Color Falls: An intermediate color falls between each primary andsecondary color.
step_by_step_procedure: Color Wheel Ready: Traditional color wheel When you are ready to paint, use the color wheel tochoose a harmonious color scheme.
Basic Wheel Colors: This basic wheel has 12 colors, a combination of primary colors (red, yellow, blue), secondary colors (green, orange, purple), and sixtertiary.
Warm Colors Wheel: The warm colors of the wheel include the reds, oranges, and yellows.
Cool Colors Include: The cool colors include the greens, blues, and purples.

pamphlet_excerpts: Care Storage Equipment: Care and Storage of Equipment The most important part of taking care of any paint applicationtool or equipment is cleaning it immediately.
Failure Cost Time: Failure to do so can cost you more time and more money spenton special cleaners, which in some cases may ruin the tool.
Brushes They Last: If you clean your brushes after each use, they will last along time.
Cleaning Few Minutes: Cleaning takes only a few minutes and saves hoursof work and, quite possibly, the cost of replacement.
step_by_step_procedure: Paint Isallowed Harden: If paint isallowed to harden in a brush, cleaning that brush becomes adifficult and time-consuming task, one that could have beeneasily avoided.
Same Brush Paint: If the same brush and paint have been used over severaldays, store the brush for the night (with most of the paintwiped off) in tightly folded aluminum.
Carefully Smooth Down: Carefully smooth down the bristlesand wrap the brush in its original packaging or heavy papertied around the ferrule.
Paint Job Requires: A good paint job requires the right equipmentand following the right procedures.

Paint Ingredients Mishandled: Paint ingredients, when mishandled, can be dangerous.
Solvents Mineral Spirits: Solvents, such as mineral spirits, xylol, and naphtha, are present in some paints and are used to reduce or thin thepaint and during cleanup.
Solvents Particularly: Solvents are particularly hazardous tothe painter and others who may be exposed to them.
step_by_step_procedure: Follow Thesame Safety: Follow thesame safety guidelines for solvents and solvent-based paints.
Inhaling Toomany Solvent: Inhaling toomany solvent vapors can make breathing difficult, loweringthe oxygen level in the body.
Work Areawell-ventilated: Always keep the work areawell-ventilated by opening all the windows.
Part Body Comes: If part of your body comes in contact with a solvent, theresult could be harmful.

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to this merit badge. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. Your research methods may include—with your parent or guardian's permission—an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Discuss with your counselor both your findings and what about this profession might make it an interesting career. (b) Explore how you could use knowledge and skills from this merit badge to pursue a hobby or healthy lifestyle. Research any training needed, expenses, and organizations that promote or support it. Discuss with your counselor what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.
